title: signal-snapshot-and-variant-plays-aug-2029
body:
Executive snapshot:

This note compiles the highest-frequency customer signals observed in support and AE threads over the past 6 weeks, converts them into small variant plays we can ship or A/B test quickly, and surfaces a small set of cross-team risks (billing surprises, onboarding friction for Private). Purpose: make it easier for Product + Eng to pick 2 low-effort, high-confidence experiments for the next two-week sprint.

Topline themes (by recurring customer impact):
1) Predictable latency at tail percentiles — customers running interactive chat (consumer-facing) and search similarity workloads report spikes at p95-p99 that cause degraded UX. Many call these "stutter" incidents.
2) Cost transparency per-route — customers want token-level, route-level cost attribution exported to their internal billing systems on a daily cadence. Current token reports are per-api-key and often too coarse.
3) Private onboarding gaps — friction points: VPC peering templates, KMS/HSM policy examples, and a step that reliably fails (KV cache prewarm step) resulting in warm-up latency on first 30 minutes.
4) Model fallback policy visibility — customers appreciate automatic fallback but want to see which variant was served and why (capacity vs. cost).
5) Streaming reliability — partial streams sometimes stop and resume; customers want deterministic markers in the stream (sequence ids) to reassemble.

Representative customer notes (anonymized) and quotes:
- "We saw 3 blips this week where the chat froze for ~1.5s and our UI dropped the connection — very obvious to users." (Fintech customer)
- "We need a daily file that maps routes to estimated token spend; we have a chargeback model internally." (Enterprise SaaS platform)
- "The private deploy docs assume too much networking knowledge — we had to escalate to an SRE to debug peering." (Healthcare customer)

Signal threads and root causes (quick map):
- Latency stutters: correlated with mixed batch sizes and occasional kernel selection fallbacks when sequence lengths spike. Potential mitigations: adaptive batching window + sequence-length-aware kernel hints.
- Cost granularity ask: product lacks per-route export; the downstream problem is customers cannot tie feature usage to engineering teams. Implementation path: add route tag to usage export + daily CSV job.
- Private warm-up fail: prewarm job assumes NFS mount timing; race condition with KV cache loader. Short-term mitigation: clear retry + a visible "cache prewarm status" endpoint in private control plane.
- Fallback visibility: trace metadata exists but not surfaced to customers. We can add a header in responses (x-rw-fallback: model-id;reason) for transparent logs.
- Stream markers: the stream currently returns token chunks without deterministic indices. Adding an incremental "chunk_id" field is low-risk and helps clients reassemble streams.

Prioritized micro-proposals (ranked by ease x impact; recommended 2 experiments):
A) Daily route-cost CSV export (owner: Elena Rossi) — scope: backend job to emit route, model_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, estimated_cost, date. Success metric: 75% of enterprise billing customers can reconcile their internal chargeback within 48h of receiving file. Estimated effort: 2 wks.
B) Stream chunk_id + resume token (owner: Jonah Kim) — scope: add chunk_id and optional resume_token in streaming payload; SDKs to expose resume hooks. Success metric: 50% reduction in customer support tickets related to resumed streams within 4 weeks. Effort: 1 week backend + 1 week SDK updates.
C) Private deploy "prewarm status" endpoint + retry helper script (owner: Priya Menon) — scope: add status API, augment onboarding docs with a shell script that polls and retriggers prewarm. Success metric: reduce Private onboarding escalations referencing "cache warm" by 60% in next onboard cohort. Effort: 1 week docs + 1 week API.
D) Fallback header for transparency (owner: Eng-serving-runtime team) — add x-rw-fallback header with model and reason; UI + Console to highlight fallback events. Success metric: customers report improved understanding in CS check-ins. Effort: small (engineer: 3 days + console: 1 week).

Quick experiment designs (lightweight):
- Experiment 1 (A vs baseline): Deploy daily route-cost CSV to 5 pilot customers. Ask them to import to their invoicing system and report a reconciliation metric after 2 billing cycles. Provide a simple sample importer script.
- Experiment 2 (B vs baseline): Roll stream chunk_id to SDK alpha channel. Provide client sample that intentionally drops and resumes stream. Measure time-to-resume and support tickets.

Edge-case flags and unanswered questions:
- Billing: per-route costs may be gamed if customers artificially split routes; need to define the canonical tag semantics and guardrails. Ask finance: should exported cost be "estimated" or "billable"? (JIRA-CCS-4821)
- Security: adding resume tokens to streams — ensure tokens are short-lived and revocable. Coordinate with security review.
- Private onboarding: the prewarm workaround improves UX but masks root issue (NFS timing race). Longer-term: explore replacing NFS dependency in prewarm flow.

Suggested prioritization rubric (for CS + Product):
- Urgency: production impact to customer UX (p99 latency stutters, streaming breaks) = high.
- Effort: 1–2 week small changes favored for Q3 micro-sprint.
- Customer reach: affect multiple enterprise customers or a single high-ARR customer = prioritize.

Ownership and next steps (recommended sprint picks):
1) Pick experiment A (daily route-cost CSV) and experiment B (stream chunk_id) for the next two-week sprint sprint. Responsible: Elena + Jonah. Kickoff: 2029-08-19.
2) Add a short-term private onboarding patch (prewarm status endpoint) as a concurrent quick-win (Priya).
3) Schedule a security review for stream resume tokens (owner: Eng-security). Timeline: 1 week.

Communication plan:
- For pilot customers we will: email a short note describing the experiment, include a "how to use" script, and schedule a 30-min feedback call 2 weeks after start. Templates: CS will use the new pilot email template (linked_artifacts: CONFLUENCE-ccs-onboarding-privates).

Appendix: quick snippets and templates (for CS to copy-paste)
- Pilot invite subject: "Pilot: daily route-cost export — 2-week trial"
- Quick email body: "We're piloting a daily CSV export that maps API routes to token usage and estimated unit cost. If you'd like to participate we'll provision access and share an importer script. The goal is to help you automate chargebacks. We'll check in after 2 billing cycles."

Unresolved items to discuss in triage (meeting agenda):
- Finance: confirm whether the export is estimated or billable and any contract implications.
- Eng-runtime: confirm how long chunk_id will be stored and whether it affects streaming latency.
- Product: finalize the pilot customer list (5 customers), prioritize across verticals (fintech, healthcare, platform).

Notes to self / CS playbook snippets:
- When customers report "warm up cold start" ask for: time-of-day, initial request size, model_id, and whether prewarm script logs show "kv:loader:ok".
- Escalation path: if private onboarding stalls >48h escalate to Solutions Eng with logs attached and prewarm status output.

Last updated by Asha Patel 2029-08-16 09:12 PT
